extracted.intended_audience: European patent applicants, patent attorneys, EPO examiners and other practitioners before the EPO
extracted.subtask_description: Applying Article 56 EPC and related EPO guidelines and case law to decide whether an invention involves an inventive step (non-obviousness) with respect to the state of the art, including treatment of technical/non-technical features and Art.54(3) documents. Covers problem-and-solution approach, formulation of the technical problem, and related case-law topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (Article 56 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention shall be considered as involving an inventive step if, having regard to the state of the art, it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory non-obviousness test under Art.56 EPC; assessment requires identification of the state of the art and the skilled person and a determination whether the claimed solution would have been obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of Article 54(3) documents from inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: If the state of the art also includes documents within the meaning of Article 54(3), these documents shall not be considered in deciding whether there has been an inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art.54(3) prior-art (European patent applications published after the priority date but before the filing date) count for novelty only and are excluded from inventive step analysis per Art.56 wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art pursuant to Art.54(3) (GL G IV 5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance topic: treatment of state of the art under Art.54(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a relevant EPO Guideline topic for inventive-step/novelty interplay; see GL G IV 5.1 for details on how Art.54(3) documents are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulation of the objective technical problem (GL G VII 5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance topic: how to formulate the objective technical problem in inventive-step analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key step in the problem-and-solution approach; guidance found in GL G VII 5.2 on avoiding hindsight and deriving the objective problem from the closest prior art and effects achieved by the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims comprising technical and non-technical features (GL G VII 5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance topic: assessment of claims that mix technical and non-technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant to deciding which claim features contribute to inventive step (technical contribution) and which should be disregarded (non-technical features / 'as such' features).

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem and solution approach (CLR I D 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: the problem-and-solution approach for assessing inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO case law standard methodology for inventive-step assessment: (i) determine closest prior art, (ii) establish objective technical problem, (iii) consider whether the claimed solution is obvious in view of the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the technical problem (CLR I D 4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: how the technical problem is determined in inventive-step proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses identification of the technical effect and derivation of the objective technical problem from the closest prior art and the claimed effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative solution to a known problem (CLR I D 4.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: assessing inventive step where the claimed invention is an alternative solution to a known problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance concerns when providing an alternative solution may or may not involve an inventive step, depending on whether the alternative would have been obvious to try.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable expectation of success (CLR I D 7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: the role of reasonable expectation of success in inventive-step assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when assessing whether the skilled person would have been motivated to combine prior art or try a course of action with a reasonable prospect of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical character of an invention (CLR I D 9.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: whether an invention has the required technical character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing technical character is a prerequisite for patentability under EPC and affects which features are considered in the inventive-step analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions having both technical and non-technical features (CLR I D 9.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: treatment of mixed inventions containing technical and non-technical elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on separating technical contributions from non-technical aspects and evaluating inventive step only on the basis of technical contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Comvik approach (CLR I D 9.1.3.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: the Comvik (mixed-type claim) approach to assessing inventive step for inventions with non-technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Comvik, non-technical features do not contribute to inventive step unless they interact with technical features to produce a technical effect; this approach is frequently cited in EPO practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-technical features and technical contribution (CLR I D 9.1.3.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: assessing whether non-technical features provide a technical contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on identifying when features typically excluded as 'non-technical' nonetheless make a technical contribution that supports an inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical implementation of excluded subject-matter (CLR I D 9.1.3.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: when an implementation transforms excluded subject-matter into a technical contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses when features implementing an otherwise excluded matter (e.g., business method, program) in a technical way can be considered in inventive-step analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: The aim to be achieved in the formulation of the technical problem (CLR I D 9.1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: role of the aim to be achieved when formulating the technical problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns use of the objective technical problem formulation to avoid hindsight and ensure only objectively derivable aims are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental activities based on data visualisation (CLR I D 9.1.6.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: treatment of mental activities or presentation of information (data visualisation) in inventive-step analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on whether and how activities that are essentially mental or relate to presentation of information can contribute to inventive step (generally excluded unless providing a technical effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of features relating to mathematical algorithms (CLR I D 9.1.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: how mathematical algorithms in claims are assessed for inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses when algorithms are to be treated as technical (contributing to inventive step) versus being excluded as purely abstract/mathematical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alleged effect not a feature of the claims (CLR II C 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: consequences when a claimed technical effect is not actually a feature of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the alleged effect relied upon for inventive step is not derivable from the claim features, it cannot generally be used to support inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 83 EPC and clarity of claims (CLR II C 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: sufficiency of disclosure (Art.83 EPC) and clarity issues that may affect assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While primarily about sufficiency/clarity, these aspects can bear on inventive-step assessment if the invention is not clearly or sufficiently disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of inventive step without assessing the prior art (CLR III K 3.4.5.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-law topic: circumstances where inventive step may be assessed without a full separate assessment of prior-art documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses procedural or methodological points in inventive-step reasoning; see case law for examples and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particularly relevant documents in search (GL B X 9.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance topic: identification of particularly relevant documents during search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates to selecting prior art literature that is especially pertinent to novelty/inventive-step analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where the invention is realised in a distributed computing environment (GL F IV 3.9.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance topic: treatment of inventions implemented in distributed computing environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant to assessing technical character and inventive step for computer-implemented inventions deployed across distributed systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad claims (GL F IV 4.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance topic: examination of unusually broad claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on when broad claim language may be objectionable or how breadth interacts with novelty/ inventive-step assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficiencies which, if not remedied, lead to opposition being rejected as inadmissible (GL D IV 1.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance topic: procedural deficiencies in opposition that can affect admissibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rules may affect whether substantive inventive-step objections are entertained in opposition proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient disclosure of the invention (GL D V 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance topic: when disclosure is insufficient under opposition procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficiency (Art.83) can be a ground for revocation separate from inventive step, but interrelates with how the invention is interpreted for inventive-step purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements of European patent applications relating to nucleotide and amino acid sequences (R.30 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule: special formal/content requirements for sequence listings and biological sequence information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant where inventions involve sequences; affects content of application and may affect prior-art/ inventive-step considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the description (R.42 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule: requirements for the description part of a European patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper disclosure in the description is necessary to support claims and can affect how technical features are understood in inventive-step analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the European search report (R.61 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule: what the European search report must contain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search report identifies relevant prior art that will be considered in novelty and inventive-step evaluation.
